paragraphs: So it is cited in Yuchasin: “Rav Bavahu said to Rav Ashi, at the end of chapter 2 of Yevamot,” and [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=663&lang=en) wrote, “I have not found it.” Hyman points to [Bava Kamma 117a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.117a.15), “Rabbi Abbahu raised an objection to Rav Ashi,” and Hyman reports the reading Rabbavahu in Dikdukei Soferim (this Rabbi Abbahu was one of the heads of the kallah of Rafram, as explained in his entry). Likewise in Yevamot 26a, the reading of the Or Zarua HaGadol is “Rabbi Abbahu said to Rav Ashi.”[^4] Hyman considers Yuchasin’s reading there too undoubtedly Rabbavahu. In [Chullin 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.49a.8), “Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Abbahu said” — Hyman reports “son of Rabbavahu” in Dikdukei Soferim. See his entry.[^3]

notes.text: Undoubtedly preserves Hyman’s force while keeping the Rabbavahu/Abbahu/Bavahu readings and proposed Yuchasin reading distinct. His head-of-kallah identification remains attributed rather than an independent identity merge.

Davidson Bava Kamma 117a directly reads Rabbi Abbahu raising an objection to Rav Ashi. Rabbavahu/Bavahu, the Or Zarua and Dikdukei Soferim readings, Rafram’s kallah identification and Hyman’s undoubtedly about Yuchasin remain distinguished, not silently merged.

The linked Chullin reads “Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Abbahu” and gives his father’s place in Rafram’s assembly. The consulted Yevamot 26a has Rav Hillel address Rav Ashi. Hyman attributes the Abbahu form there to Or Zarua. Heilprin preserves the Yevamot reference and says he did not find it.

The same exchange at [Yevamot 26a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.26a.5) begins with Rav Hillel addressing Rav Ashi. This is the consulted Bavli form. Rabbi Abbahu is Hyman’s report of the Or Zarua reading, and Rabbavahu is his reconstruction of Yuchasin’s reading.
